name: High-Density Polyethylene
common_uses: Plastic bottles, corrosion-resistant piping, geomembranes, plastic lumber, bottle crates, fuel jerrycans
notes: Chemically inert, odorless, colourless solid with high strength-to-density ratio; can withstand up to 120C for short periods. No plasticizers or phthalates in pure HDPE. Standard handling: process below degradation range, ventilate melt fumes.

name: Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene
common_uses: 3D printing filament, automotive interior trim, consumer electronics housings, LEGO bricks
recyclability: Recyclable but often downcycled; resin identification code 7
notes: Tough, impact-resistant thermoplastic. Processing temperatures ~220-260C. Emits styrene and acrylonitrile vapours if overheated; ensure ventilation. Not suitable for food contact without certification.

name: Polyethylene Terephthalate
common_uses: Beverage and food bottles, rigid and flexible packaging, polyester textile fibre, photovoltaic module backsheet
recyclability: Most widely recycled plastic (resin identification code 1)
notes: Insoluble in water, practically inert in normal use. Degrades above processing temperatures - can release acetaldehyde; the Wikipedia article documents an antimony discussion section. Avoid overheating beyond stated melting range.

name: Polypropylene
common_uses: Packaging and containers, textiles and reusable bags, automotive parts, medical devices, laboratory equipment
recyclability: Recyclable (resin identification code 5); recycling rates lower than PET/HDPE
notes: Toughest commodity plastic by weight (lowest density 0.895-0.93 g/cm3). High chemical resistance. Combustible like other hydrocarbons - ventilate when processing.

name: Low-Density Polyethylene
common_uses: Plastic bags, plastic wrap, trays and containers, dispensing bottles, tubing, six-pack rings, coated paperboard cartons
recyclability: Resin identification code 4; recyclability limited - EPA-estimated 5.7% recycled in the US (2018 figure cited by Wikipedia)
notes: Flexible and tough, chemically unreactive at room temperature except to strong oxidizers; service limit 65C continuous / 90C short-term. Melt temperature not verified in session sources (left blank).

name: Polystyrene
common_uses: Foam packaging (EPS), meat trays, yogurt pots, vacuum-formed cups, insulation boards (XPS)
recyclability: Resin identification code 6; rarely recycled through curbside schemes
notes: Figures refer to isotactic PS melting point (~240C); common amorphous PS softens near its glass transition (~100C) and has no sharp melting point. Health note: styrene monomer and fire-hazard sections documented on the source page; foam is flammable.

name: Polyvinyl Chloride
common_uses: Pipes and fittings, electric cable insulation, window frames and construction profiles, signage, flooring
recyclability: Resin identification code 3; recyclability low - chlorine content and additives complicate sorting and reprocessing
notes: SAFETY: heating or burning PVC releases hydrogen chloride (HCl) gas - a corrosive respiratory hazard per the NIOSH Pocket Guide (https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/npg/npgd0332.html). Degrades before a clean melt; melt_temp_c intentionally left blank. White, brittle solid, density 1.4 g/cm3, insoluble in water and ethanol.

name: Polyamide
common_uses: Textiles (nylon), automotive components, gears, ropes, kitchen utensils, sportswear
recyclability: Resin identification code 7; mechanical recycling possible but limited, often downcycled
notes: Synthetic polyamide includes Nylon 6 and Nylon 6-6; high durability and strength. Heating can release caprolactam and other amide fragments - ventilate melt fumes and avoid overheating. Not recommended for repeated hot food contact without testing.

name: Polycarbonate
common_uses: Safety glasses, CD/DVD blanks, automotive glazing, electrical housings, water bottles
recyclability: Resin identification code 7; recyclable but limited, often downcycled
notes: SAFETY: polycarbonate is derived from bisphenol A (BPA). Potential BPA leaching with heat and repeated use; avoid hot liquids and prolonged thermal exposure. Glass transition ~147 C; processing can release phenolic vapours - ventilate.

name: Poly(methyl methacrylate)
common_uses: Acrylic sheets, safety glass substitutes, display cases, lighting diffusers
recyclability: Resin identification code 7; recyclable but limited, often downcycled
notes: Transparent thermoplastic also known as acrylic glass. Common trade names Perspex, Plexiglas, Lucite. Density 1.18 g/cm3 per Wikipedia infobox. Glass transition ~105C, processing ~160-230C. Avoid overheating to prevent monomer release; ensure ventilation.

name: Polyethylene terephthalate glycol
recyclability: Recyclable but often downcycled; resin identification code 1
notes: Transparent amorphous polyester copolymer with glycol modification; good impact resistance and clarity. Processing ~230-260C. Avoid overheating; ensure ventilation.

name: Thermoplastic Polyurethane
common_uses: Footwear, seals, adhesives, medical devices, coated fabrics
recyclability: Elastic polymer with high abrasion resistance; melt processable; commonly used in footwear soles and automotive seals.

name: Polylactic Acid
common_uses: 3D printing filament, compostable packaging, disposable cutlery, food containers
notes: Bioplastic derived from fermented plant starch. Degrades in industrial composting conditions; not home-compostable in short timescales. Process below degradation range; ensure ventilation for melt fumes.

name: Polyetheretherketone
common_uses: Aerospace components, medical implants, high-performance engineering parts
notes: High-performance thermoplastic with excellent thermal and chemical resistance. Glass transition ~143 C. Processing requires temperatures above 360 C; ensure high-temperature ventilation and protective equipment. Not for general recycling streams.
